things.name: Spider

must_show: A spider's body is in two parts joined by a small cylindrical section.
A spider's rear body part is soft and shaped like an egg.
A spider has eight legs.
A spider has short, movable spinnerets at the back that give out silk.
A spider's body is covered with bristles that sense touch and chemicals.
not_this: A spider does not have antennae on its head.
features: A spider's body is in two parts joined by a small cylindrical section.
The front part of a spider's body is covered on top by a single rounded shell.
A spider's rear body part is soft and shaped like an egg.
A spider has eight legs.
A spider has no antennae.
A spider has four pairs of eyes on the top-front of its body.
A spider has short, movable spinnerets at the back that give out silk.
A spider's whole body is covered in a shell made of chitin and proteins.
A spider's body is covered with bristles that sense touch and chemicals.
Spiders that hunt without webs have dense tufts of fine bristles between the claws at the tips of their legs.

things.name: Scorpion

must_show: It has a pair of grasping pincers.
Its body is divided into three parts: the front cephalothorax, the abdomen called the mesosoma, and the tail called the metasoma.
The tail is divided into five segments plus the stinger part at the end.
Its body is covered by a hard exoskeleton that protects it.
features: A scorpion has eight legs.
It has a pair of grasping pincers.
Its tail is narrow and made of segments, usually curved forward over its back, and ends in a stinger.
Its body is covered by a hard exoskeleton that protects it.
Its body is divided into three parts: the front cephalothorax, the abdomen called the mesosoma, and the tail called the metasoma.
It has two eyes on top of the front part of its body and usually two to five pairs of eyes along the front corners.
Its mouth parts at the front are pincer-like, with three segments and teeth.
The tail is divided into five segments plus the stinger part at the end.
The stinger is curved and has sensory hairs on it.
It has comb-like pectines on the underside of its body that it uses as sense organs.

things.draw: A whole scorpion with a hard exoskeleton, its body in three parts: front cephalothorax, middle abdomen, and a narrow tail of five segments ending in a stinger, curved forward over its back; two grasping pincers in front, eight legs, sandy brown

things.name: Tick

must_show: A tick's body is ovoid or pear-shaped.
A tick's head-part and body are completely joined together.
A hard tick has a hard shield on its back called a scutum.
When a tick is not moving, its legs stay folded tightly against its body.
features: An adult tick is about 3 to 5 mm long.
A tick's body is ovoid or pear-shaped.
A tick has eight legs.
A tick's body swells up with blood when it feeds.
A tick's head-part and body are completely joined together.
A hard tick has a hard shield on its back called a scutum.
A hard tick has a beak-like part at the front holding its mouthparts.
A soft tick's mouthparts are on the underside of its body, so you cannot see them from above.
Most ticks are plain brown or reddish brown.
A tick's legs have seven segments and end in a pair of claws.
A tick's legs often have sensory or tactile hairs on them.
When a tick is not moving, its legs stay folded tightly against its body.

things.draw: A small eight-legged tick with a pear-shaped body, its head and body fully joined, a hard shield on its back, and legs folded tightly against its body, drawn whole in brown on plain ground

things.name: Tarantula

must_show: The two body parts are joined by a narrow waist-like piece called the pedicel.
A tarantula has eight legs, two chelicerae with fangs, and pedipalps, all attached to the front body part.
The fangs point downward.
The spinnerets are at the end of the abdomen.
The body is covered in bristles called setae.
features: A tarantula's body has two main parts: the front part (prosoma) and the abdomen (opisthosoma).
The two body parts are joined by a narrow waist-like piece called the pedicel.
A tarantula has eight legs, two chelicerae with fangs, and pedipalps, all attached to the front body part.
Each leg has seven segments.
The fangs point downward.
The chelicerae sit just below the eyes and in front of the mouth.
The eyes are small and usually set in two rows of four.
The spinnerets are at the end of the abdomen.
Tarantulas have two or four spinnerets.
The body is covered in bristles called setae.
Many tarantulas have a dense covering of irritating bristles called urticating hairs on the abdomen.
Tarantulas are large and often hairy spiders.

things.draw: A large hairy spider with eight legs, two fangs pointing down, and pedipalps on its front body, joined by a narrow waist to a big abdomen with spinnerets at its end, all covered in bristles, standing on the ground

things.name: Mite

must_show: Its body is simple and not divided into segments.
The two body parts are fused, and only where the legs are shows where the segments were.
At the front is a retractable feeding part made of the chelicerae, the pedipalps and the mouth cavity.
Most mites have four pairs of legs.
The upper surface of the body is covered with hardened plates.
features: A mite is very small, usually less than one millimetre long.
Its body is simple and not divided into segments.
Its body has two parts, a front part and a rear part, that are joined together.
The two body parts are fused, and only where the legs are shows where the segments were.
At the front is a retractable feeding part made of the chelicerae, the pedipalps and the mouth cavity.
Most mites have four pairs of legs.
Each leg has six segments.
The upper surface of the body is covered with hardened plates.
The underside of the body is covered with hardened plates.
The body and legs carry bristles called setae.
Mites are usually some shade of brown.
The genital opening is on the underside between the fourth pair of legs.
